Since our last edition great improvements have been shewn in our track performances, the most notable being that of Dave Mitchell when winning the L.C.C.

In the junior events Dave Mitchell ( of whom we shall be hearing a great deal) won the 220, 440 and 880 yds. all in good times. A programme of childrens races, presided over by Bill Lucas, gave a real family flavour and provided a welcome break for tea during the proceedings.

Another junior whose future looks bright is Dave Mitchell who put up a personal best time in winning the L.C.C. Junior Half Mile Championship very cleverly from a good class field.

In the 440 Dave Mitchell was second in 53.4 whilst Alan Jackson won the second string event in 53.5. A very good performance came from John Thresher who finished third in the 'half' in 1m.59.7s.In the second string event Dave Taylor was second in 2m.9s.

Dave Mitchell and John Thresher, both of whom are new arrivals to the senior ranks, each narrowly missed qualifying for the 800m final. They both ran very spirited races and in a couple of seasons time should prove to be outstanding performers.
Mclean, D.

Dave Mitchell won a well judged quarter in the good time of 52.1 and Alan Black obtained further points by finishing 4th in the 880. Mal Robinson won an exciting mile in 4:23.2 after a ding-dong last lap struggle with Colin Wilson (S.L.H.).

Other good performances were made during the heats on Friday evening by Alan Jackson, with a 51.8 quarter and by Dave Mitchell (another fine prospect) who did a personal best of 1:56.6 in his 880 yds heat.

Dereck Johnson ran as he liked to win the 880 yards, moving away from the field at 660, at which point our Dave Mitchell was lying second only to fade badly over the last furlong, and record 2:01 for 6th place.
The first leg, an 880, was run by Dave Mitchell and he handed over to Alan Jackson some twenty yards behind Linford (T.V.H.) and Frank Wright, running for the Police.

Dave Mitchell and Dudley Gordon both reached the final of the 880 where Dave was narrowly beaten by Haith of the Valley. In the mile John Thresher ran particularly well to gain third place in 4:26.0 behind Pegley and Darchambaud (S.L.H.) 4:23.0 and finish in front of Mal Robinson.

Dave Carter performed well to finish 4th in the 220yds final, and Terry Newell and Dave Mitchell both qualified for the final of the 880yds; but nothing of note was produced. 1961 showed us a marked absence of "Claret and Gold".
Dave Mitchell was another to have an off day recording a mediocre 2:1.7. Jim McGrath reached the long jump final and with a leap of 22'3¾" finished sixth.

Another to break a Club record at the same meeting was David Cocks, whose 2:0.8 clocking in the Intermediate 880 final was 0.2 secs inside Dave Mitchell's four year old mark, but was still not good enough to place him in the result!

With half a lap to go in the 880yds, defending champion John Davies looked an odds-on winner, but in the final straight first Terry Newell and then Dave Mitchell sprinted past, leaving a surprised John to finish fourth just behind Bhatia who had made up a tremendous amount of ground in the last 220yds.
Beats Dave Mitchell's 4yr old mark by one fifth of a second. Since setting this new time he has clocked 1:59:0 off scratch in a handicap race, so his official mark is already in danger.
